## 🔴 High Relevance (Score 7–10)
*Auto-added to Zotero (threshold ≥6)*

**[Dopamine-induced mitochondrial dysfunction activates cGAS-sTING to drive IL-6 secretion in macrophages.](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42858253)** *(from Neuroimmunology / neuropharmacology (dopamine signaling in innate immunity))*  
*Daniali Marzieh; Channer Breana; Curley Erin O; Amirfallah Amirali; Kist Taylor* —  2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NF-kB-IKK, mito-ROS-NF-kB, treatment-target, ME-CFS, other`  
> Shows in primary human macrophages that mitochondrial depolarization leads to mtDNA release into the cytosol, which activates cGAS-STING and NF-kB to drive IL-6. This closely mirrors the Loop A (mtDNA escape → cGAS-STING) and NF-kB crosstalk axes of the SAMHD1 A565T model, and the pharmacological inhibition at several nodes has treatment implications. The trigger is dopamine, a neuro-immune link that could bear on the family's AuDHD and ME/CFS phenotypes, but the paper has no SAMHD1, dNTP, NLRP3 or interferon data, so the connection is mechanistic and indirect.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118118

Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NLRP3, treatment-target, clinical-phenotype, other`

This closely mirrors the Loop A to NLRP3 axis and supports cGAS/STING/NLRP3 as treatment targets, but it has no SAMHD1, dNTP, VDAC1 or ISG15 data. Its link to the family phenotype is indirect, through possible ocular involvement (glaucoma and cataract-adjacent eye disease) and the shared mtDNA-cGAS-NLRP3 mechanism.  
DOI: 10.1038/s41420-026-03382-7
